title: Partially-Full Interval Rate Volatility
pattern: Upscaling rate calculations inside an incomplete measurement window based on the elapsed time of a partial interval.
why_bad: During the first few seconds of a window, upscaling causes extreme metric volatility. A single transaction at second 1 registers as "60 requests per minute," triggering false alarms on rate threshold dashboards before quickly collapsing to normal rates.
detection: Look for rate calculations multiplying partial counts by `total_window_time / partial_elapsed_time`.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. If traffic is guaranteed to be completely uniform, upscaling is accurate, but real traffic is bursty.
strength: Strong` — guarantees severe noise and metric spikes during initial window phases.
source: Richard L. Sites - *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Chapter 9.8, p. 152-154.
